channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: NPC-Forge: build conversational agents with zero ML — hands-on with the deterministic, CPU-only agent framework
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: NPC-Forge is a deterministic, CPU-only conversational-agent framework with no ML and no LLMs: a 24,000-intent terminal assistant, a built-in test suite, and an OpenAI-compatible gateway that serves every NPC as a model. Install it, test it, and build your own tool-calling NPC in one JSON file.

item.title: Boston Dynamics gave Atlas a new pair of hands — and Reddit is arguing about the missing pinky
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: The new generation hand for Atlas has four fingers, 13 degrees of freedom, dense tactile sensors, and no pinky. The accompanying Boston Dynamics blog post explains exactly why — and the r/singularity thread that surfaced the video within hours went straight for the missing digit.

item.title: SoftBank wires the final $10B to OpenAI: Son's cumulative bet hits $64.6B for a 13% stake
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: SoftBank Group executed the third and final $10 billion tranche of its OpenAI follow-on investment on October 1, completing a $30 billion commitment unveiled in February. Son’s cumulative bet now stands at $64.6 billion for roughly 13% of the ChatGPT maker — funded by what Reuters calls the largest junk-bond sale in history.

item.title: XPENG takes the G9L global at the Paris Motor Show: its “AI flagship SUV” runs VLA 2.0 — and brings a robot lineup
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: XPENG announced today it will give its G9L — billed as a “Next-Gen AI Flagship SUV” running its VLA 2.0 model on the in-house Turing AI chip — its global launch at the 2026 Paris Motor Show on October 12, opening European order books alongside a “Physical AI” showcase of humanoid robots, flying cars, and live autonomous test rides with Tesla.

item.title: Hire an AI red team for the price of an API key: hands-on with Strix, the 65K-star autonomous pentesting agents
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Strix (usestrix/strix) sends autonomous AI agents to hack your app inside a Docker sandbox and reports only vulnerabilities they have proven with a working exploit. We installed 1.6.2, mapped every CLI flag, built a deliberately vulnerable target and proved its holes, and wired the CI gate — command by command.

item.title: ZoomInfo launches Agent Teams: AI agents that run the whole sales play — built on yesterday’s DoubleO.ai buy
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: ZoomInfo announced today Agent Teams, AI agents that run complete go-to-market plays from signal to action without human babysitting — built on the DoubleO.ai orchestration startup it acquired yesterday, available now in GTM Studio with no new SKU or contract.

item.title: Ptarmigan-1: Talus Bio's AI skips protein folding to drug the 'undruggable' — 5,000x faster screening
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Talus Bio released Ptarmigan-1 today, the first AI model to predict small-molecule binding across the entire human proteome without ever modeling a 3D structure — screening 3.4 billion compounds in a day and reaching the roughly 40% of proteins that folding-based tools can't touch.

item.title: Apple's new CEO John Ternus plots an overhaul: faster launches, leaner teams, and a more experimental AI push
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: One month into the job, Apple CEO John Ternus is laying out a plan to break the company's sacred spring-and-fall launch rhythm, cut layers of management, and make Apple more experimental for the AI era — according to a new Bloomberg report.

item.title: OpenRig: run Claude Code and Codex as one persistent agent team — hands-on with the 3,300-star multi-agent harness
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: OpenRig (mvschwarz/openrig) turns Claude Code, Codex, and Pi into persistent teams — roles, shared context, owned work — defined in one YAML file and launched with rig up. We installed @openrig/cli 0.6.3, previewed its setup plan, started the daemon, inspected the starter teams, and planned a two-agent launch, command by command.

item.title: Mandiant founder Kevin Mandia’s Armadin raises $255.5M: an AI attack swarm valued over $2.5B
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Armadin, the AI-native cybersecurity startup led by Mandiant founder Kevin Mandia, has raised $255.5 million at a valuation over $2.5 billion — seven months after emerging from stealth, its autonomous agent swarms are already running attack campaigns for Fortune 500 enterprises and governments.

item.title: Get decisions with real probabilities from any open LLM: a hands-on guide to AnyJev
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: AnyJev (nokia-applied-research/AnyJev) is the Apache-2.0 toolkit that turns any open LLM into a Jev-style decision model: typed choices, yes/no and score questions with probabilities you can actually threshold. Truncate a Qwen to two-thirds depth, serve it with vLLM, and fit a closed-form head from 100-300 labels — auto-decidable traffic goes from 7.7% to 52% at 5% risk. Every command verified against the project's own docs.

item.title: Pi: the 110,000-star open-source coding agent you can point at any model
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Pi (earendil-works/pi) is the MIT-licensed open-source coding agent climbing GitHub trending: a unified multi-provider LLM API, a scriptable headless agent loop, and BYO-model support via a single models.json. Install 0.99.2, wire it to your own endpoint, and watch it write and read files — every command ran exactly as shown.

item.title: Synthesia launches Sessions: AI avatars you can talk back to — Roleplay and Survey live today
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Synthesia launched Sessions on October 1, 2026: a ready-made platform for real, two-way conversations with lifelike AI avatars. Roleplay and Survey Sessions are available from today; Expert Sessions is coming soon.

item.title: Herdr: run every coding agent in one terminal — hands-on with the 41K-star Rust multiplexer
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Herdr is a 41K-star Rust terminal multiplexer rebuilt for the agent era: a background server keeps your coding agents’ terminals alive, marks each one working, blocked, or idle, and exposes everything over a socket API you can drive headlessly. Install it, build a three-pane dev rig, and survive a server restart — every command verified.

item.title: “AGI achieved”: the 29-second AI meme montage r/ChatGPT can’t stop arguing about
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A 29-second AI-generated montage of internet memes — ‘Meme York City’ — pulled nearly 1,900 upvotes on r/ChatGPT under the joking banner ‘Funny AGI achieved.’ The top comments refused the joke and graded the real thing: scene consistency.

item.title: Infrastructure AI launches "Agentic Asset Valuation": AI agents to price buildings from live operations data
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Infrastructure AI introduced Agentic Asset Valuation on October 1, 2026: governed AI agents on its Galaxy Agentic Operating System translate live building-operations data into continuously updated financial signals for owners, lenders, insurers, and investors.

item.title: Health In Tech launches HitRix: AI document intelligence for the $1T self-funded health insurance market
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Health In Tech (Nasdaq: HIT) launched HitRix on Thursday, an AI-powered platform that takes the paperwork out of large-group health insurance submissions — while telling investors the payoff won’t show up until 2027.

item.title: MuleSoft's founder raises €106M to back Europe's AI foundations: DIG Ventures bets the plumbing wins
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: DIG Ventures, the London venture firm founded by MuleSoft's Ross Mason, closed a €106 million ($120 million) Fund III on Thursday to back 30 pre-seed and seed startups building the data, identity, compliance, and orchestration layers underneath enterprise AI.

item.title: Connecticut's AI law goes live today: whistleblower shields for lab workers, written consent for ChatGPT renewals
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Connecticut's Act Concerning Online Safety takes effect today: whistleblower protections for frontier-lab workers, written consent for AI subscription renewals, and risk-management duties for the biggest models.

item.title: LoopGain: stop your agent loop the moment it actually converges — hands-on with the control-theoretic cost controller
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: LoopGain is an Apache-2.0 Python library that replaces max_iterations with a control-theoretic stop-and-rollback policy: it watches your loop's error trajectory, stops the moment it converges, and rolls back to the best iteration. Install it, run the verified examples, and wire it into any verify-revise loop.

item.title: Google DeepMind launches Gemini 4 Argon: 1M-token outputs, cyber defenders first, and half of Claude's price
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Google DeepMind's first Gemini 4 model can generate up to a million tokens in a single response, is rolling out first to cyber defenders through the Fairwind Program, and undercuts its rivals on price. The benchmarks look strong — with a few conspicuous exceptions.

item.title: Stop letting your coding agent grep: hands-on with CodeGraph, the 72K-star pre-indexed code knowledge graph
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: CodeGraph (72,600+ GitHub stars) pre-indexes your codebase into a local SQLite knowledge graph — symbols, call edges, imports — so your coding agent answers architecture questions in one explore call instead of forty grep-and-Read round-trips. We installed v1.6.1, indexed a real project, ran every query that matters, and wired the MCP server into an agent.

item.title: See exactly what your coding agents cost: hands-on with Agent Console, the 765-star local-first token dashboard
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Agent Console (765 GitHub stars, MIT) reads the transcripts Claude Code and Codex already write on your machine and turns them into a local dashboard: tokens by class, per-model cost estimates, live burn rate, and spend alerts — no account, no telemetry, no build step. Installed v0.4.1 from source and from the signed release, walked the demo, pointed it at real sessions, joined a second machine to a team hub.

item.title: IBM Bob goes air-gapped: IBM's agentic coding platform now runs inside the data center
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: IBM's agentic coding platform Bob can now run self-hosted — on-premises, in sovereign clouds, and air-gapped — so regulated enterprises can use AI agents without their code leaving the building.

item.title: Your agents can't talk to each other: build two interoperating agents with the A2A protocol — hands-on
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: A2A (Agent2Agent) is the Linux Foundation's open protocol for agent-to-agent communication: MCP connects agents to tools, A2A connects agents to each other. We built two real interoperating agents with the official Python SDK 1.2.1 — a FactFinder research agent and a BriefWriter that delegates to it — covering agent cards, the task lifecycle, artifacts, and true delegation. No API key, no GPU; every command verified.
